recommendation: Keep the core audit as-is. Future Patient/$everything corrections should be made in HL7/admin-incubator, with core changed only if the external link target changes.
issue_request: FHIR-13919 was Published/Persuasive for STU3 and asked to clarify Patient/$everything for use against multiple patients by relaxing the old single-patient error wording from "should return an error" to "may return an error" and adding bulk/asynchronous-access notes.
initial_application: The Jira comment records svn revision 12810. In git, e434b7bc7b (#13919 - bulk data documentation) changed the Patient $everything spreadsheet source to one-or-more-patient wording, introduced the may-return-error behavior for no nominated patient, and added asynchronous and bulk data guidance.
additional_context: Patient is still an active core resource, but the current Patient operations list no longer includes OperationDefinition/Patient-everything. Commit b487fdda4b removed Patient-everything from core and rewired active core links to the HL7 Admin Incubator continuous build. The external Admin Incubator Patient/$everything definition still says the operation covers one or more patients, uses all patients available to the requesting user for GET /Patient/$everything, permits returning an error instead of all records, and notes async/bulk-format handling. FHIR-44816 later synced Encounter/EpisodeOfCare $everything with the Patient version and already has a combined-branch audit commit.
reconciliation: Published an empty external-repo audit commit. The authoritative Patient/$everything operation is now outside this checkout, and the external current operation already satisfies the seed resolution; reintroducing or duplicating Patient/$everything text in core would be a scope regression.
